acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — Terraform provisions one S3 event bucket per environment, named events.{env}.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com where {env} is the short environment name (dev or prod), with: versioning enabled, all four public-access-block flags set to true, server-side encryption AES256 (SSE-S3), and a lifecycle configuration that transitions current objects to STANDARD_IA at 90 days and GLACIER_IR at 365 days but never expires a current version.

verification.definingInputProperty: A real applied bucket in the development environment, not a plan preview
verification.assertions: get-bucket-versioning Status == Enabled; all four public-access-block flags true; SSEAlgorithm == AES256; lifecycle contains transitions at 90d STANDARD_IA and 365d GLACIER_IR and contains no Expiration member on current versions

verification.definingInputProperty: A real applied bucket in the production environment
verification.assertions: Same property set as the development bucket; proves the per-environment scope word in the criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — A three-level delegated Route53 topology exists, mirroring the established soulofyoga.fifthdimensionengineering.com precedent: (1) a product zone personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, delegated from the existing parent zone fifthdimensionengineering.com by an NS record set (TTL 300); (2) a development zone dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, delegated from the product zone by an NS record set (TTL 300); (3) a production zone prod.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, delegated from the product zone by an NS record set (TTL 300). No zone's auto-created apex SOA/NS record set is managed by Terraform.

verification.definingInputProperty: All three zones applied, with delegation records written into the parent and product zones respectively
verification.assertions: Each of the three zones exists; each has an NS record set at TTL 300 in its delegating parent whose values equal that zone's name_servers; no aws_route53_record of type SOA or apex NS is declared in the configuration

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — Remote state uses the pre-existing shared state bucket terraform.tfstate.us-west-2.fifthdimensionengineering.com (region us-west-2) with encrypt = true and use_lockfile = true for native S3 locking. No DynamoDB lock table and no bootstrap module are created. State keys are fifthd-personal-events/{shared|dev|prod}/terraform.tfstate — one key per root, never shared.

verification.definingInputProperty: A backend block naming the pre-existing shared bucket with use_lockfile enabled
verification.assertions: init succeeds against the shared bucket; the three roots resolve three distinct state keys
No DynamoDB lock table argument anywhere and no bootstrap module directory — the negative half of the criterion

acceptanceCriteria.explicitUserApproval: Supersedes the prior DynamoDB/bootstrap acceptance criterion. Approved by user 2026-08-31.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — For every root module (shared, development, production): terraform fmt -check -recursive passes, terraform validate passes, terraform plan completes with no errors, and a second terraform plan run after terraform apply reports No changes. — i.e. zero drift, with no perpetual diff on lifecycle rules or NS record sets.

verification.command: for d in shared development production; do terraform -chdir=infra/environments/$d plan -detailed-exitcode || exit 1; done
verification.definingInputProperty: A plan executed AFTER a completed apply, across the complete set of three roots
verification.assertions: -detailed-exitcode returns 0 (no diff) for every root; exit code 2 indicates drift and fails this criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — After apply, dig +short NS personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, dig +short NS dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, and dig +short NS prod.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com each return the nameservers of the corresponding created zone — resolved from the public DNS system, not merely present in the Route53 API.

verification.definingInputProperty: Resolution through the public DNS system after NS propagation, not a Route53 API listing
verification.assertions: dig +short NS returns a non-empty nameserver set for each of the three zones, equal to that zone's name_servers Terraform output

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — Inputs are parameterized via variables (aws_region, aws_profile, env, project_name, parent_domain); no account id, domain, region or environment string is inlined in a resource body. Outputs expose, per environment: event bucket name and ARN, the environment zone id, and its name_servers.

verification.assertions: Output JSON contains event_bucket_name, event_bucket_arn, environment_zone_id, environment_zone_name_servers

verification.definingInputProperty: The module directory, where no literal domain should appear
verification.assertions: No hardcoded domain in any module resource body — the counterexample proving parameterization rather than mere variable existence

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — The inherited parent_domain defect is fixed: parent_domain is fifthdimensionengineering.com and project_name is personal-events, so the zone name interpolation produces dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com and not the currently-configured duplicated development.simple-eventer.simple-eventer.fifthdimensionengineering.com. var.env carries the short name (dev/prod) per .agents/guidance/deployment-environments/aws.md, while the environment directories retain their long names (development/, production/).

verification.definingInputProperty: The planned zone name string, taken from plan output rather than from the variable defaults
verification.assertions: The exact fully-qualified name dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com appears in the plan

verification.definingInputProperty: The whole infra tree including tfvars
verification.assertions: The duplicated/legacy name is entirely absent — counterexample against a fix applied in only one of the several places the string appears

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — Failure modes, each producing a clear, actionable message rather than a crash or a silent partial apply: missing or expired AWS credentials → plan fails naming the credential problem; a parent_domain whose zone does not exist → the data "aws_route53_zone" lookup fails with a message naming the missing zone; a bucket name longer than 63 characters → caught by a validation block on the variable, at plan time, not by an AWS API error; re-running apply with no source change is idempotent (no resource replaced).

verification.assertions: Non-zero exit and an error message naming the credential/profile problem

verification.definingInputProperty: A parent domain with no corresponding Route53 hosted zone
verification.assertions: Non-zero exit; the error names the missing zone rather than failing later during apply

verification.definingInputProperty: A project_name long enough to push the derived bucket name past S3's 63-character limit
verification.assertions: Rejected by the Terraform variable validation block at plan time, with the length named — not by an AWS API error at apply time

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-09 — Guidance conformance: HCL is split one-responsibility-per-file with no catch-all main.tf; every environment/account value is a variable (.agents/general.md "Infrastructure conditionals are not domain code"); terraform fmt is clean; any helper shell script passes shellcheck.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete infra tree and every helper script
verification.assertions: fmt reports no files needing formatting; shellcheck reports zero warnings
